content: The DMAC1 transmembrane protein 261 is a protein in humans encoded by the TMEM261 gene, which is located on chromosome 9. This gene is also referred to as C9ORF123, DMAC1, Chromosome 9 Open Reading Frame 123, and Distal Membrane-Arm Assembly Complex Protein 1. The gene spans 91,891 base pairs on the reverse strand. Another gene on the reverse strand in close proximity encodes protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type delta. The TMEM261 gene contains two exons and one intron, and it produces six primary transcript variants. The largest mRNA transcript variant is 742 base pairs long and encodes a protein of 129 amino acids with a molecular weight of 13,500 Daltons. The smallest coding transcript variant is 381 base pairs long and encodes a protein of 69 amino acids with a molecular weight of 6,100 Daltons. Structure The TMEM261 protein contains a domain of unknown function, DUF4536 (pfam15055), which is predicted to be a helical membrane-spanning domain approximately 45 amino acids in length (Cys47-Ser92). This domain does not have any known relationships to other domains. Additionally, two other transmembrane helical domains are predicted, one spanning 18 amino acids (Val52-Ala69) and the other spanning 23 amino acids (Pro81-Ala102). A low-complexity region spanning 25 amino acids (Thr14-Ala39) is also present. The tertiary structure of TMEM261 has not yet been determined, but its secondary structure is predominantly composed of coiled-coil regions, with beta strands and alpha helices located within the transmembrane and DUF4536 regions. The N-terminal region of TMEM261 is disordered and includes the low-complexity region, which is not highly conserved among orthologues. Modifications An N-myristoylation domain is present in most TMEM261 protein variants. Post-translational modifications include myristoylation of the N-terminal glycine residue (Gly2) and phosphorylation of threonine at position 31. Interactions TMEM261 interacts with several proteins, including NAAA (protein-protein interaction), QTRT1 (RNA-protein interaction), ZC4H2 (DNA-protein interaction), and ZNF454 (DNA-protein interaction). It also interacts with APP (protein-protein interaction), ARHGEF38 (protein-protein interaction), and HNRNPD (RNA-protein interaction). Predicted transcription factor binding sites include one for MEF2C, a monocyte-specific enhancer factor involved in muscle-cell regulation, particularly in the cardiovascular system, and two for GATA1, a globin transcription factor involved in erythroblast development. Expression TMEM261 is ubiquitously expressed in humans and is detected in nearly all tissue types. It exhibits tissue-enriched gene (TEG) expression compared to housekeeping gene (HKG) expression. The highest expression levels are observed in the heart (94% relative expression), particularly in heart fibroblast cells, the thymus (90% relative expression), and the thyroid (93% relative expression), particularly in thyroid glandular cells. Cancer cell staining shows intermediate to high expression in breast, colorectal, ovarian, skin, urothelial, and head and neck cancer cells. Function The function of TMEM261 is currently unknown. However, gene amplification and rearrangements of its locus have been associated with various cancers, including colorectal cancer, breast cancer, and lymphomas. The primary structure of TMEM261 shows higher conservation in mammals, with the DUF4536 domain and the C-terminal region being highly conserved across all orthologues, including distant homologues. The protein structure of TMEM261 is conserved across most orthologues. Paralogues TMEM261 has no known paralogues.
